Why are Indian investors increasingly looking at US stocks instead of limiting themselves only to the Indian stock market?
Is it just about returns, or is there a bigger business model story behind companies like Apple, Google, and Amazon?

In this detailed business model case study, we break down why US stocks are attracting Indian investors, and what makes American companies structurally different from most Indian listed firms. From global revenue diversification and strong pricing power to innovation-driven growth and dollar-based earnings, this video explains the real reasons behind the growing interest of Indians in the US stock market.

We closely analyze how Apple’s ecosystem, Google’s advertising dominance, and Amazon’s platform-led business model create long-term wealth for shareholders. You’ll understand how these companies scale globally, manage risks better than region-focused businesses, and why they are often considered safer long-term bets by Indian investors.

This video also explains:

Why US stocks offer exposure to global brands

How currency (USD vs INR) plays a role in long-term returns

Why Indian investors want diversification outside India

What makes US stock market investing attractive for beginners and long-term investors

How business model strength matters more than short-term stock price movement

If you are someone who wants to understand why Indians invest in US stocks, how US companies build global monopolies, and what lessons Indian investors can learn from Apple, Google, and Amazon, this case study will give you clarity beyond surface-level investing advice.

Whether you’re a beginner exploring US stock market investing from India or a long-term investor looking to understand business fundamentals, this video will help you think like a global investor.
